$comment: Patches applied to the vendored pylabview WHEN THE BUNDLE IS ASSEMBLED, never to vendor/ itself.
That keeps VENDOR.md's 'local changes: none' true of the vendored tree, so an upstream fix can
still be taken by copying the package over it. provision.ps1 applies these; a Find string that
does not occur EXACTLY ONCE is a hard error, because the failure mode to avoid is a patch that
silently stops matching after an upstream change and leaves the bug back in.
ANCHOR A FIND SO THAT THE UPSTREAM FIX BREAKS IT. A Find matching a line upstream's own fix
leaves untouched will keep applying after that fix lands, stacking a redundant change and
raising no error - which is the exact drift these entries claim to prevent. Span the lines the
Each entry: File relative to app/, Find and Replace as exact strings, Why, and Upstream.

tdProbeTable = self.getTopType(probeTable_typeId, section_num=section_num)

patches.why: getNumRepeats() is called on the probe table without checking that it IS a RepeatedBlock. Only TDObjectRepeatedBlock defines that method, so a VI whose probe table resolves to a Cluster, Number or NumberPtr dies with AttributeError and extracts NOTHING - readRSRC exits 1 with zero files, not a partial bundle. The crash is in cosmetic code (setPurposeText and setDataFillComments only add XML comments), so no content was ever beyond reach. Measured on a production codebase: 32 of 900 VIs, all with this one cause - 28 Cluster, 3 NumberPtr, 1 Number - all of them DQMH module VIs. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS NOTE ADDED 'which is why NI's own example corpus never hit it'. That is false, and it mattered, because it made the bug sound like it needed a customer's code to see. It does not: the DQMH examples SHIPPED WITH LABVIEW reproduce it on a stock install - measured 2026-08-25 by swapping this file for the vendored original, on examples/Delacor/Delacor QMH/DQMH Fundamentals - Thermal Chamber/Libraries/Device Under Test_Cloneable_DQMH/Addressed to This Module.vi: upstream exits 1 with 0 files and an AttributeError, patched exits 0 with 19 files. Swept whole: 108 of the 240 VIs under vi.lib/Delacor and examples/Delacor are affected - 45%, against 3.6% in the production codebase - and they show FOUR wrong types, not three: 101 Cluster, 5 Ptr, 1 Boolean, 1 AlignedBlock. Ptr, Boolean and AlignedBlock are types no probe table could legitimately be, which is the strongest evidence yet that probeTable_typeId simply lands on an arbitrary entry. The earlier census never walked the add-on example trees. THE FORM BELOW IS THE MAINTAINER'S OWN, taken verbatim from his reply on issue #40 (2026-08-25): normalise tdProbeTable to None where it is resolved, and warn at verbose > 1 naming the file and the unexpected type. It is behaviourally identical to the guard-at-use form it replaces - tdProbeTable has no other consumer in commentSpecialTypes - but the warning is not cosmetic: he reads three different wrong types as evidence that the probeTable_typeId computation or the DSINIT entry positions are wrong for some versions, not that probe tables legitimately vary. Under that reading a silent guard hides a real bug, while -vv prints the evidence needed to chase it. TD_FULL_TYPE is imported function-locally at LVblock.py:5841 and eprint at module level, so the snippet compiles where it sits.
patches.upstream: reported as mefistotelis/pylabview#40; the maintainer approved this form but said he is not willing to spend time on it, so it may sit unmerged. Remove this entry once it lands upstream - the Find spans the two lines his fix inserts between, so provision will fail loudly rather than stack a second guard.

patches.why: Reader, writer and XML form of what LabVIEW writes after a class link record's API link cache content (UDClassAPILinkCache): u32 N, N x (qualified name, path ref, u8) - the class's ancestors, nearest first; a u8; and from file version 20 u32 M, M x (qualified name, path ref, u32 K, K x (qualified name, path ref)) - a class with its parents, filled only by a type cast's TCPI (Panel.lvlib: Reference Position <- Window Position, Ref Display <- Reference Position). Nothing in it is aligned, an empty PTH0 still carries its tp and count as LVPath0 already reads it, and a VIPI is followed by nothing, so the next nextLinkInfo can sit at an odd offset. Decoded 2026-10-12 over the class link records of NI's examples on this station (509 VIs with a class link, raw sections pylabview had left as binary): 1249 records of file versions 17, 20 and 26 walk exactly onto the next record's nextLinkInfo with this layout, VIPI, TCPI, FPPI, DDPI, DyOM, VRPI and PNOM alike; only the 37 records of three LabVIEW 8.2 files do not, and upstream reads none of those either. Patched, 497 of those 509 VIs (all but the twelve 8.2 ones) extract with no LI block left binary and rebuild with every LI section byte-identical; before, 140 LIvi and 138 LIbd blocks stayed binary. THE PREVIOUS ENTRIES (class-link-cache-extra-*) READ A FIXED 8 BYTES AND PADDED TO EVEN: N, the byte and three of M's four bytes, the fourth supplied by the padding - right only while N and M are 0 and the content length is even, which held for every VI built here and failed on 140 LIvi and 138 LIbd blocks of NI's own examples ('List of LinkObjects incorrectly ended with 1 after VIPI' wherever a class has a parent - every Actor Framework actor). The u8 is 0 in a VIPI and a TCPI's 0 or 1, and in heap records takes ASCII-looking values (ff, 20, 61, 6e, 74, 75) and changed on every LabVIEW 2026 Save for Previous of one VI, so it is kept verbatim (APILinkTailByte), not interpreted. APILinkExtra from an older extract is still read when its entries are empty.
patches.upstream: not reported yet - the layout is LabVIEW 2016 and later, newer than upstream's samples. Remove the class-link-tail entries together once upstream reads it.

patches.why: Clears the decoded tail with the rest of the cache, so a record built from XML or cleared for reuse never serialises a previous record's ancestors (part of class-link-tail-helpers).

patches.why: Reads the tail (class-link-tail-helpers) from file version 16. Upstream reads straight on into the offset list or the next record, so a DyOM answers 'Offset List length 16711680 exceeds limit', a VIPI 'List of LinkObjects incorrectly ended with ...', and the WHOLE block falls back to raw binary. BOTH BOUNDS ARE BRACKETED by composing one class caller (t128) under each version stamp and loading it in LabVIEW 2026, each arm with and without the part in question: 15 loads only WITHOUT the tail and 16 only WITH it; 19 loads only without M and 20 only with it (14 fails either way, for some other reason). NI's examples agree - 11 version-13 VIs carry no tail, 141 version-17 records carry N and the byte and no M. LabVIEW 2026's Save for Previous goes back to 2025 only, so it could not settle either bound. 8.2 files fail before this point, as upstream.
patches.upstream: not reported yet - the layout is LabVIEW 2016 and later, newer than upstream's samples. Remove the class-link-tail entries together once upstream reads it.

patches.why: The TCPI record, which upstream does not know: LIbd's link from a type cast on the diagram (To More Specific Class and its kin) to a class - LabVIEW.exe names it HeapTypeCastToUDClassAPILinkRef beside the HeapObj-, DDO- and DynInfo- links pylabview has. Its layout is the HeapObj one: basic link save info, the API link cache with its tail, then the offset list. Without it every block holding one answers 'contains path data of unrecognized class' or 'unrecognized class b\'TCPI\'' and stays binary - 138 LIbd blocks of NI's examples, Actor Framework launchers and LUnit and LMock tests among them.

patches.why: DataFillTypeDef.initWithRSRCParse names an undefined `client` in its error handler, so ANY failure while reading a typedef's default data surfaces as `NameError: name 'client' is not defined` and the real exception is lost. The sibling class a few hundred lines up writes sub_td.fullType(), which is what is meant. Found through issue #96 (2026-10-21), where it hid the variant-consolidation fault below for a whole diagnosis: the user's report and the first run on NI's Simple Network Streams example both showed only the NameError and a later TypeError on TDObjectTag.ident. The Find spans the -1/tm_flags call above the handler because the corrected line alone already occurs in the sibling class, which provision.ps1 then reads as 'already present' and skips - measured on the first provisioning of this entry.
patches.upstream: not reported yet - a one-word fix, report together with the variant-consolidation entries.

patches.why: ROOT CAUSE of issue #96 (Network Stream endpoints). A variant that is part of a TYPE DESCRIPTOR - the LVVariant inside a TDObjectTag - stores its types inline (varcount + TDs) instead of as VCTP indices, and pylabview reads it so. But a variant in the DEFAULT DATA of such a variant was always created with useConsolidatedTypes=True, so it read a varcount as a VCTP index, found no type there, and raised `LVVariant has no linked TD but is supposed to have DataFill` - upstream's own comment at that spot reads 'the lack of use of ConsolidatedTD should be propagated'. A Network Stream endpoint refnum is exactly that shape: its tag's NI_VAR_DATATYPE attribute holds the stream's data type with a default value, and a cluster element of type Variant (NI's own Simple Network Streams example streams cluster{string Message, variant Message Data}) puts a nested variant in it. The TDObjectTag then aborted before reading its ident, and checkSanity died on len(None). Measured 2026-10-21 on that example (LabVIEW 2026): unpatched readRSRC exits 1 with 0 files for Host and Target; patched it extracts 39 and 34 files, rebuilds, and the rebuilt VIs re-extract to byte-identical XML in every file. Paired with variant-consolidation-rsrc and -xml, which raise the counter.
patches.upstream: not reported yet - fixes upstream's own TODO in LVclasses.LVVariant.parseRSRCVariant. Remove the three variant-consolidation entries together.

patches.why: Read half of variant-consolidation-inherit: while a variant whose types are inline (not consolidated) reads its default data, every DataFillLVVariant created underneath - at any depth of cluster or array - inherits useConsolidatedTypes=False. A counter on the VI rather than a parameter, because the nested fills are built through newDataFillObjectWithTD several classes away, none of which takes a flag.

XML half of variant-consolidation-inherit, so a REBUILD writes the nested variant back in the inline form it was read in. Without it the extract succeeds and the rebuild writes a VCTP index where LabVIEW expects a type list. Measured as the round trip in variant-consolidation-inherit: rebuilt Host and Target re-extract identically.
